readings: Matching examinations to their patients, count the examination records for each `SEX` value (blank and missing sexes are their own groups) and work out each sex's share of the combined count. Among the sexes whose count is above the average count per sex, give one row with the total of their counts, the average of their shares, and the average amount by which their counts exceed that per-sex average.
queries:
WITH c AS (
  SELECT p.SEX AS SEX, COUNT(*) AS cnt
  FROM Examination e
  JOIN Patient p ON e.ID = p.ID
  GROUP BY p.SEX
),
t AS (
  SELECT SEX, cnt,
         CAST(cnt AS REAL) / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share,
         AVG(cnt) OVER () AS avg_cnt
  FROM c
)
SELECT SUM(cnt) AS total_count,
       AVG(share) AS avg_share,
       AVG(cnt - avg_cnt) AS avg_excess
FROM t
WHERE cnt > avg_cnt;
